comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures report Gaming segment financial performance for fiscal year 2024. In contrast to NVIDIA's disclosure of $10.4 billion in Gaming revenue representing a 15% increase year-over-year driven by new product launches (GeForce RTX 4060/4070, SUPER GPUs), AMD reports Gaming net revenue of $2.6 billion, a significant decrease of 58% from the prior year. The divergence is attributed to different product cycles: NVIDIA benefited from strong demand for its Ada Lovelace architecture, whereas AMD's decline was primarily driven by lower semi-custom product revenue.

In Gaming, we launched the GeForce RTX 4060 and 4070 GPUs based on the NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architecture.

The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue.
